_what: Human-verified ground truth for audio-only (scriptless) QC. Every entry was confirmed by a person LISTENING to the audio, not derived from any tool output. This file exists because that knowledge previously lived only in commit messages and chat, which is how two changes shipped on plausible reasoning and had to be reverted (local-drift 982485c, and the relative-only music gate that killed a verified drop).
_how_to_use: python -m tests.score_ear_truth <report.json> <case-id>. A change is only an improvement if verified_missing recall does not fall AND false_flag count does not rise. Flag COUNTS alone are noise: identical inputs have produced 28-48 transcript lines and, before the VAD-window change, two identical EP41 runs shared 1 of 8 flags.
_provenance: Verdicts given by the studio-side user (pmo@rian.io) in Audacity, 2026-07-30 and 2026-08-03, against drift-aligned window pairs. tolerance_s is how close a flag must land to count as a hit.

ep38-mix.description: EP38 full episode, Hindi ST_MIX vs Tamil ST_MIX. One grunt-class drop at 699.8 (2026-08-04). AUDIO drift-map says this pair is aligned to ±0.2s everywhere — all earlier ±20s 'drift' was text-alignment artifact. Script-QC ground truth does NOT apply here: the studio patches lines before mixing, so lines missing from the stems are audibly present in the delivered mix (proven on EP41 and EP42). Re-listen also confirmed the Tamil runs slightly BEHIND the Hindi (matches the measured +5.8s local drift).

ep41-stems-VOID.description: PLANNED GT CASE, VOIDED 2026-08-03 before adoption: EP41 Hindi premix vs today's summed Tamil stems. Script-QC (July) recorded 12 lines missing from the stems, but the studio RE-DELIVERED PATCHED STEMS since — the user ear-confirmed the 'snacks cafe Hidamari' line audible in the current stems sum. The production build's 2/12 'recall' was CORRECT behaviour against current audio. THIRD instance of stale ground truth masquerading as a tool failure. RULE: ground truth derived from a delivery is only valid against that exact delivery (pin by Box sha1).
